name: Uzza
overview: The name Uzza appears in Scripture associated with multiple individuals and a significant location. Notably, Uzza is the proprietor of a burial garden where kings Manasseh and Amon were laid to rest, highlighting a role of custodianship over royal sepulchers (2 Kings 21:18, 21:26). Additionally, Uzza is identified as a son of Shimei in the genealogies of the Levite family of Merari (1 Chronicles 6:29), and as a son of Ehud in another lineage (1 Chronicles 8:7). The name also appears among the Nethinim, a group set apart for temple service, as seen in the post-exilic lists in Ezra and Nehemiah (Ezra 2:49; Nehemiah 7:51). These references collectively present Uzza as both a person of familial significance and as a figure connected to sacred duties and royal heritage.
